capabilities: Speak selected text with a floating Play button or a command palette command
Stop synthesis or playback with a Stop button or command
Configure speech speed, variation, and seed in settings
Cache model graphs and runtime assets locally for offline playback
Synthesize in a background worker so the editor stays responsive
extras: First run downloads roughly 38 MB of model graphs plus runtime assets from jsDelivr and the official owensong/Inflect-Micro-v2-ONNX export; the model provides one fixed English male voice and is not voice cloning or multilingual. The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
intentEvidence: Hosted TTS services require an account, an API key, and a copy of your writing on somebody else's server.
motivation: The author wanted to hear selected passages without uploading writing to somebody else's server, and without provider configuration, a Python runtime, or a local server.
problem: Hosted TTS services require accounts, API keys, and sending note content to a third-party server; Obsidian has no built-in private, offline speech synthesis.

relations.evidence: it bundles ephone, an eSpeak-NG WebAssembly frontend under GPL-3.0-or-later
Local Voiceover adapts the browser port of Inflect Micro v2 into an Obsidian plugin

summary: Text-to-speech plugin that speaks selected note text locally with the Inflect Micro v2 model via ONNX Runtime, with no API key or account.
